text: Whoa, what was that. Wait, why do I hiccup?
There's a muscle called the diaphragm - the one you breathe with - and it just twitches on its own, whether you want it to or not.
But right as that breath rushes in, your throat reflexively clamps shut for an instant. That's the sound you hear.
Most hiccup fits end in seconds or minutes, but the record holder reportedly hiccupped for sixty-eight years straight.
There's also a saying that holding your breath stops hiccups - build up enough carbon dioxide, and the spasm supposedly calms down.
